title: Egyptian Revolution of 2011 (25 January Revolution)
summary: In 18 days from 25 January 2011, millions of Egyptians took to the streets against Hosni Mubarak. On 1 February an estimated 2 million people protested in Tahrir Square, Cairo. On 11 February the vice-president announced that Mubarak had resigned and handed power to the army. Amnesty reports at least 840 people killed and 6,467 injured, citing Ministry of Health sources.

uncertainty.note: Amnesty counts 18 days, day 18 being 11 February.

where.historical_name: Tahrir Square, Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt

importance.justification: Toppled a ruler of nearly three decades and became a landmark of the 2011 Arab uprisings.

audience_note: Describes deaths and injuries of protesters and detentions and torture. Casualty counts are official or NGO figures.
